en: Look closely: is the orphan boy Semetey
More of a hero than I?
Among the Argyn and Ogoy peoples,
I dwelt in Talas;
This army of mine deceived six times
His proud father Manas.
Your Talas is no such land;
The orphan you praise,
Look closely, is no greater hero than I!
When my wrath takes hold,
My black horse flies soaring;
While my dear head remains,
It is my custom to strike
The eighteen thousand worlds to powder.
Accursed Azhybay,
Do not babble and provoke my rage.
If you will give the maiden, say so;
If not, state your answer.
Tell me the fortress for which you girded your waist;
If you will not give her, tell your truth!
Over Chürök, whom you refuse when asked,
I shall cast a cold lasso;
Chürök, whom you refuse though I desire her,
I shall seize and drag away.
If I stiffen and wrath takes hold,
If you do not accept what I say,
If you do not give Aychürök,
I shall dig a well in your place of honor
And hang a cauldron upon your breast;
I shall scatter all your four kinds of livestock.
If you resist, Azhybay,
I shall open your eyes wide as flour dumplings!
When I came besieging, you said, 'I shall give her';
Your oath has expired, Azhybay.
Speaking much falsehood and truth,
Your affliction has gone too far, Azhybay.
You will accept what I say,
And you will give Aychürök.
If I leave you freely in your place,
You say there is a khan greater than me,
You say there is a son of Manas.
Semetey and I are kinsmen,
Born equal at the same window;
Our villages were together in Talas.
To tell the truth, Azhybay,
Aychürök is the wife I shall take.
Speaking evasive words,
You wretch, where have you wandered?
When I grow angry, Aychürök
Is the widow I myself shall take.
If he rages and fights,
I myself shall slaughter
That fugitive son of Manas,
And I myself shall meet
The hell that comes from it!
If you do not abandon your treachery,
Hear my words now, my Azhy:
If you truly provoke my wrath,
I shall trample your hearth,
Overrun you without ceasing,
And leave none of your stumps;
I shall finish and wipe them all away.
If you provoke my rage, Azhybay,
I shall overrun your Afghanistan!
If you will give her, tell the truth;
If you will not, say so.
Without scheming, you Azhy,
Name the ridge where we shall cross spears,
Tell me the place where we shall exchange gunfire?"
As Kozho stood surging with fury,
Then Azhy said this.
Broad-jawed and flat-tongued,
Unfaltering Azhybay,
Honking like a young goose,
Warrior Azhy began his speech
And let it pour out with a cackle:
"What you have said is also true,
Stallion Kozho, leopard;
All that you have said is true.
It is also true that I did not accept
The words you spoke at first.
It is also true that I withheld Chürök,
Out of fear of the final turmoil,
And did not give her.
It is also true that with eloquence
I began speaking many words,
Deceived you six times,
And abandoned you.
If these words of yours are true,
Warrior Kozho, leopard,
I shall accept what you demand;
I shall give you all
The maidens whose heads are pledged.
You are indeed a hero, warrior Kozho;
Now I know your true nature.
If you are starved of women,
I shall give them all together,
Even the wife in my embrace.
You are indeed a hero, Kozho;
Now I recognize your mastery.
I shall gather and give you
Every maiden among my people!
I have become your in-law, true Kozho;
Now I understand your words.
You will take Chürök, daughter of Akun,
In a few days;
Speak your truth before you leave!
And again, Kozho, turn back
And do not let your fury seize you.
State your grounds openly;
Tell me, Chynkozho,
Which of you two is the husband who will take her!
Toltoy and Chynkozho,
Whichever of you goes, let that one go;
You have strength enough for one man.
Eat meat from one platter,
And fit yourselves into one bed;
Come back without letting your destination grow old,
And return within seven days!
I shall prepare your sleeping place;
If Chürök says she will not marry,
I shall bind her with a carrying sling."
Hearing those words Azhybay spoke,
Kozho went mad,
And gulped like a rabid dog.
Raging and surging,
He spoke with renewed courage:
"If this Toltoy is unworthy,
Accept what I demand;
If you do not favor Toltoy
To take as a husband,
Then give her directly to me!"
Tümönbay, son of Tülkü,
A harsh, blustering hero,
His seizure taking hold as his soul burned,
Unable to remain standing, surged forward.
Tümönbay stood and spoke:
"You frantic Zhediger,
Whispering two by two,
What have you now said?
Do not babble, Zhediger;
Does a man flee from combat?
If you flee, you have eaten filth!
You swagger, Chynkozho;
If you take Aychürök as plunder,
Will she become wife to all of you?
Accursed Zhediger,
Is that precious child Aychürök
To become wife to all of you?
Accursed Chynkozho,
God bears witness to your violence;
Does the man who gives you a daughter prosper?
You strain and surge without cause;
Can a Muslim be like you?
Is it right to call
A fool like you a Muslim?
I shall not give the maiden—do what you can!
Accursed Chynkozho,
If you cannot do it, take your mother!
Take the lint from my pocket;
You seem to have grown excited—
Take the root of a great prick!
If you are offended, take my sheath;
Here, accursed one, I shall give you
The handle of my battle-axe!
Hey, bastard Chynkozho!
You have no Argyn people in Talas;
I shall not give the maiden—take this of mine!
Do not rattle without cause.
Is Tümönbay a man who lets a pair pass,
Or is Tümönbay the black earth?
Is Tümönbay now less
Than a fugitive who wanders fleeing?
I have given Chürök—take her husk;
Here, I shall make it tribute:
Take the root of my cunning!
Your people may be many,
And my people may be grass;
You may possess spears—
Do I possess only a poker?
For the waist you have girded,
Come out with resolve, Kozhokul,
To the place where we shall exchange shots!
Rejecting good words for wickedness,
Take your mother instead of Chürök!"
When they call him "Kozho, Kozho,"
Does he not swell with pride,
And like a male black crow
Begin hopping about!
Like a black-faced young ram,
Do you not grow swollen with pride?
Like a tethered yearling colt,
Do you not begin prancing?"
Roaring and shouting,
Bending the tops of the apricot trees,
Flame shooting from his eyes,
And smoke billowing from his mouth,
He seized a black-edged battle-axe
And made himself ready.
Straining like a white tiger,
As he was about to send
The pretentious Kozho over the hill,
About to make dust whirl in confusion,
And spill mottled red blood,
As ruin was about to break out,
Azhybay, son of Azhy,
Such was his wisdom:
"He will send the pretentious Kozho
Over the hill," he thought;
"This pig who struck from above
Will be left disgraced."
As he was about to make the tale compelling,
Toltoy and Chynkozho,
And the swarming Zhediger—
As he was now about to deceive them,
"God has taken the fool;
He has begun the ruin now," he thought.
Azhybay struggled to intervene,
Quarreling with Tümönbay.
Raging and straining,
From the other side Chynkozho
Now stood surging forward,
Beating the earth as he strained,
And surging in anger.
Toward devil-ridden Kozho,
He now stood surging,
And spoke to Tümönbay:
"You are a hero, Tümönbay;
Your heroism has become clear.
Like a wolf among sheep,
Your ferocity has become clear.
Among your many devils,
Your greatness has become clear.
Like iron placed in fire,
Your hardness has become clear.
You have surged too far, Tümönbay;
Have you brought on my rage?
Accursed Afghan,
Shall I cut one of you down!"
Chynkozho stood surging,
And put on armor no bullet pierced;
If you had seen Chynkozho,
He strained like a blue bull.
He made ready to take up
His golden-edged battle-axe;
He roared in anger,
Shouting the cry, "Alaman!"
Tölök struggled there,
Quarreling with Chynkozho:
"Fool struck from above!"
When pure God was about to grant
The rattling Afghans to you,
When the Afghans, drawn by the spectacle,
Were now about to come before you,
Why did God strike you
So you reel in frenzy?
